from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any

from abc import abstractmethod
from system.message import Info
from system.message import BaseMessageDataType
from model.strategy_type import StrategyType
from model.base import BaseStrategy

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes_list = data['nodes']  # list of int
        edges_list = data['edges']  # list of tuples
        
        # Sort nodes for consistency
        sorted_nodes = sorted(nodes_list)
        
        # Build the graph for original G (bad interactions)
        graph_G = self._build_graph(sorted_nodes, edges_list)
        
        # Find all maximal independent sets using Bron-Kerbosch on complement
        maximal_sets = []  # list to store the maximal cliques in complement, i.e., independent sets
        self._bron_kerbosch(sorted_nodes, graph_G, set(), set(sorted_nodes), set(), maximal_sets)
        
        # Convert to sorted lists of cocktails
        maximal_cocktails = [sorted(list(cock)) for cock in maximal_sets]  # each cocktail is sorted
        
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            num_maximal_cocktails = len(maximal_cocktails)
            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,
                difficulty=message.difficulty,
                message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=num_maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
            )
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,
                difficulty=message.difficulty,
                message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
            )
    
    def _build_graph(self, nodes: list, edges: list) -> dict:
        graph = {node: set() for node in nodes}
        for u, v in edges:
            if u != v:  # prevent self-loops
                graph[u].add(v)

    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes_list = data['nodes']
        edges_list = data['edges']
        
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            maximal_cocktails_list = self.get_maximal_cocktails(nodes_list, edges_list)
            num_maximal_cocktails = len(maximal_cocktails_list)
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            maximal_cocktails = self.get_maximal_cocktails(nodes_list, edges_list)
            # For normal, we set maximal_cocktails as per template
            # But in the return, we use it directly in the data
        
        return Info(
            sender=self.__class__.__name__,
            receiver=message.sender,
            difficulty=message.difficulty,
            message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=num_maximal_cocktails if message.difficulty == 'easy' else maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
        )
    
    def get_maximal_cocktails(self, nodes_list: List[int], edges_list: List[tuple]) -> List[List[int]]:
        # Build adjacency list
        adj = collections.defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges_list:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)
        
        # Sort nodes for fixed order
        nodes_sorted = sorted(nodes_list)
        all_nodes_set = set(nodes_sorted)
        
        # List to store results
        result = []
        
        def backtrack(pos: int, current_set: set):
            if pos == len(nodes_sorted):
                # Check maximality: all nodes not in current_set must have at least one neighbor in current_set
                not_in_set = all_nodes_set - current_set
                if all(any(neighbor in current_set for neighbor in adj[node]) for node in not_in_set):
                    # Add a sorted list of the current set to results
                    result.append(sorted(list(current_set)))
            else:
                v = nodes_sorted[pos]
                # Choice to not include v
                backtrack(pos + 1, current_set)
                # Choice to include v only if not adjacent to any in current_set
                if current_set.isdisjoint(adj[v]):
                    backtrack(pos + 1, current_set | {v})
        
        # Start backtracking from position 0 with empty set
        backtrack(0, set())
        return result

from pydantic import BaseModel

from model.strategy_type import StrategyType
from model.base import BaseStrategy

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes_list = data['nodes']
        edges_list = data['edges']
        
        # Sort nodes for consistent order and remove duplicates if any
        nodes = sorted(set(nodes_list))
        n = len(nodes)
        
        # Create index mapping
        node_index = {node: idx for idx, node in enumerate(nodes)}
        
        # Build adjacency list for indices
        adj_list = [set() for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges_list:
            if u in node_index and v in node_index:
                idx_u = node_index[u]
                idx_v = node_index[v]
                if idx_u != idx_v:  # avoid self-loops
                    adj_list[idx_u].add(idx_v)
                    adj_list[idx_v].add(idx_u)
        
        # Generate all independent sets using backtracking
        ind_sets = []  # list of sets of indices
        def backtrack_ind(pos, current_set):
            if pos == n:
                ind_sets.append(current_set.copy())
                return
            # Do not include node at pos
            backtrack_ind(pos + 1, current_set)
            # Include node at pos if not adjacent to any in current_set
            if all(neigh not in current_set for neigh in adj_list[pos]):
                # Add pos to current_set
                current_set.add(pos)
                backtrack_ind(pos + 1, current_set)
                # Remove pos after recursion
                current_set.remove(pos)
        
        # Start backtracking with empty set
        backtrack_ind(0, set())
        
        # Define function to check if a set is maximal
        def is_maximal(S_set):
            for i in range(n):
                if i not in S_set:
                    if adj_list[i].isdisjoint(S_set):  # no adjacency to S_set
                        return False
            return True
        
        # Find all maximal independent sets
        maximal_ind_sets = [S for S in ind_sets if is_maximal(S)]
        
        # Convert back to original nodes and sort each cocktail
        maximal_cocktails = [[nodes[idx] for idx in sorted(S)] for S in maximal_ind_sets]
        
        # Determine output based on difficulty
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            result_data = len(maximal_cocktails)
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            result_data = maximal_cocktails
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unknown difficulty")
        
        return Info(
            sender=self.__class__.__name__,
            receiver=message.sender,
            difficulty=message.difficulty,
            message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=result_data, type='custom')]
        )

        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT

        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes_list = data['nodes']
        edges_list = data['edges']

        nodes = sorted(set(nodes_list))
        n = len(nodes)
        
        # Create index mapping
        node_index = {node: idx for idx, node in enumerate(nodes)}
        
        # Build adjacency list for indices
        adj_list = [set() for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges_list:
            if u in node_index and v in node_index:
                idx_u = node_index[u]
                idx_v = node_index[v]
                if idx_u != idx_v:  # avoid self-loops
                    adj_list[idx_u].add(idx_v)
                    adj_list[idx_v].add(idx_u)
        
        # Generate all independent sets using backtracking
        ind_sets = []  # list of sets of indices
        def backtrack_ind(pos, current_set):
            if pos == n:
                ind_sets.append(current_set.copy())
                return
            # Do not include node at pos
            backtrack_ind(pos + 1, current_set)
            # Include node at pos if not adjacent to any in current_set
            if all(neigh not in current_set for neigh in adj_list[pos]):
                # Add pos to current_set
                current_set.add(pos)
                backtrack_ind(pos + 1, current_set)
                # Remove pos after recursion
                current_set.remove(pos)
        
        # Start backtracking with empty set
        backtrack_ind(0, set())
        
        # Define function to check if a set is maximal
        def is_maximal(S_set):
            for i in range(n):
                if i not in S_set:
                    if adj_list[i].isdisjoint(S_set):  # no adjacency to S_set
                        return False
            return True
        
        # Find all maximal independent sets
        maximal_ind_sets = [S for S in ind_sets if is_maximal(S)]
        
        # Convert back to original nodes and sort each cocktail
        maximal_cocktails = [[nodes[idx] for idx in sorted(S)] for S in maximal_ind_sets]
        
        # Determine output based on difficulty
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            result_data = len(maximal_cocktails)
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            result_data = maximal_cocktails
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unknown difficulty")
        
        return Info(
            sender=self.__class__.__name__,
            receiver=message.sender,
            difficulty=message.difficulty,
            message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=result_data, type='custom')]
        )

from pydantic import BaseModel

from model.strategy_type import StrategyType
from model.base import BaseStrategy
from collections import defaultdict

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        # nodes_list is a list of nodes in integer
        nodes_list = data['nodes']
        # edges_list is a list of tuple, and the two values in tuple are integer means there is an edge between these two nodes
        edges_list = data['edges']
        
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            # return the number of maximal cocktails in integer
            num_maximal_cocktails = None
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            # return the maximal cocktails in a list of list, and each inner list means a disjoint cocktail list in integer
            maximal_cocktails = None

        # Build adjacency list
        adj = defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges_list:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)  # undirected graph

        # Define recursive function to find all maximal independent sets
        def find_all_maximal_independent_sets(current_nodes: set) -> list:
            if not current_nodes:
                return [tuple()]  # empty tuple for empty set
            v = min(current_nodes)  # choose the smallest node for determinism
            # Neighbors of v within current nodes
            neighbors_v = adj[v].intersection(current_nodes)
            # Closed neighborhood of v
            Nv_closed = {v} | neighbors_v
            # Remove closed neighborhood
            S_minus_Nv = current_nodes - Nv_closed
            # Maximal independent sets that contain v
            mis_with_v_base = find_all_maximal_independent_sets(S_minus_Nv)
            mis_with_v = [tuple(sorted([v] + list(T))) for T in mis_with_v_base]
            # Maximal independent sets that do not contain v
            S_minus_v = current_nodes - {v}
            mis_without_v_base = find_all_maximal_independent_sets(S_minus_v)
            # Filter those that are adjacent to v
            mis_without_v = [T for T in mis_without_v_base if any(u in neighbors_v for u in T)]
            # Combine both parts
            all_mis = mis_without_v + mis_with_v
            return all_mis  # list of sorted tuples

        # Get all maximal independent sets for the full graph
        all_mis_tuples = find_all_maximal_independent_sets(set(nodes_list))

        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            num_maximal_cocktails = len(all_mis_tuples)
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            maximal_cocktails = [list(tup) for tup in all_mis_tuples]  # convert tuples to lists

        return Info(
            sender=self.__class__.__name__,
            receiver=message.sender,
            difficulty=message.difficulty,
            message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=num_maximal_cocktails if message.difficulty == 'easy' else maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
        )

Rules
-----
1. In this game, drugs are represented as nodes in a graph.
2. Harmful interactions between drugs are represented as edges connecting nodes.
3. A **cocktail** is a set of drugs with **no harmful interactions** among them.
4. A **maximal cocktail** is a cocktail where **no more drugs can be added** without introducing a harmful interaction.
5. In the **easy level**, you need to calculate **the number of maximal cocktails**.
6. In the **normal level**, you need to **list all maximal cocktails** explicitly.

Drugs = [1, 2, 3, 4]

  - [2, 3, 4]

So:
- In **easy level**, the number of maximal cocktails is **2**.
- In **normal level**, the maximal cocktails are **[[1, 3, 4], [2, 3, 4]]**.

----
Implement a Python strategy that, given the current `nodes_list` and `edges_list`, returns the correct result based on difficulty level.

**Input Format:**  
- `nodes_list`: a list of integers, representing the drugs.  
- `edges_list`: a list of tuples, where each tuple (u, v) means drugs `u` and `v` have a harmful interaction.

**Output Format:**  
- If difficulty is `'easy'`: Return an integer, the number of maximal cocktails.  
- If difficulty is `'normal'`: Return a list of lists, each inner list is a maximal cocktail.

        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT

            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

        nodes_list = data['nodes']
        edges_list = data['edges']
        
        # Create node to index mapping
        node_to_index = {node: idx for idx, node in enumerate(nodes_list)}
        n = len(nodes_list)
        
        # Create adjacency list for indices
        adj = [set() for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges_list:
            idx_u = node_to_index[u]
            idx_v = node_to_index[v]
            if idx_u != idx_v:  # Avoid self-loops
                adj[idx_u].add(idx_v)
                adj[idx_v].add(idx_u)
        
        # Full nodes as sorted tuple of indices
        full_nodes = tuple(range(n))
        
        # Define the recursive function to find all maximal independent sets
        def all_MIS(node_tuple):

            v = node_tuple[0]  # Choose the first node

            nodes_not_in_Nv = tuple(u for u in node_tuple if u != v and u not in adj[v])

            MIS_not_containing_v = [S for S in MIS_G_minus_v if any(u in adj[v] for u in S)]
            # Total MIS
            total_mis = MIS_with_v + MIS_not_containing_v
            return total_mis
        
        # Get the list of maximal independent sets in indices
        mis_index_list = all_MIS(full_nodes)
        
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            num_maximal_cocktails = len(mis_index_list)

            receiver=message.sender,

from abc import abstractmethod
from system.message import Info
from system.message import BaseMessageDataType
from model.strategy_type import StrategyType

from collections import defaultdict

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes_list = data['nodes']  # list of integers representing nodes
        edges_list = data['edges']  # list of tuples representing edges
        difficulty = message.difficulty
        
        # Build adjacency list using defaultdict for efficient neighbor lookup
        adj = defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges_list:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)  # Ensure undirected graph
        
        # Define a recursive function to find all maximal independent sets
        def find_maximal_indep_sets(verts):
            if not verts:
                return [[]]
            # Sort the vertices to maintain consistent order
            verts = sorted(verts)
            v = verts[0]
            verts_without_v = verts[1:]  # Remaining vertices after removing v, still sorted
            # Find maximal independent sets in the subgraph without v
            mis_without_v_sub = find_maximal_indep_sets(verts_without_v)
            # Filter those sets where v is adjacent to at least one node in the set
            mis_not_contain_v = [S for S in mis_without_v_sub if bool(set(S) & adj[v])]

            vert_set = set(verts)
            closed_N_v = {v} | (adj[v] & vert_set)

            remaining_vertices_set = vert_set - closed_N_v
            remaining_vertices = sorted(list(remaining_vertices_set))
            # Find maximal independent sets in the remaining subgraph
            mis_in_remaining = find_maximal_indep_sets(remaining_vertices)
            # Create maximal sets containing v
            mis_contain_v = [[v] + t for t in mis_in_remaining]
            # Combine all maximal independent sets and sort each one
            all_mis = mis_not_contain_v + mis_contain_v
            all_mis_sorted = [sorted(mis_set) for mis_set in all_mis]
            return all_mis_sorted
        
        # Compute the maximal cocktails for the whole graph
        maximal_cocktails = find_maximal_indep_sets(nodes_list)
        
        if difficulty == 'easy':
            # Return the number of maximal cocktails
            num_maximal_cocktails = len(maximal_cocktails)
            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,
                difficulty=message.difficulty,
                message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=num_maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
            )
        elif difficulty == 'normal':

            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,

from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
from enum import Enum
from abc import abstractmethod

from system.message import Info
from system.message import BaseMessageDataType
from model.strategy_type import StrategyType
from model.base import BaseStrategy
from collections import defaultdict

class CountMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy:
    def __init__(self, model: BaseStrategy):
        self._model = model
        self.name = self._model.name
        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
    
    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def receive_message(self, message: Info) -> Info:
        data = message.message[0].data
        nodes = data['nodes']  # list of integers
        edges = data['edges']  # list of tuples
        
        # Create adjacency list
        adj = defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)  # undirected graph
        
        # Sort nodes for fixed order
        node_list = sorted(nodes)
        n = len(node_list)
        
        if message.difficulty == 'easy':
            # Count the number of maximal cocktails
            count = 0
            
            def backtrack(index, S):
                nonlocal count
                if index == n:
                    # Check if S is maximal
                    if all(any(neighbor in S for neighbor in adj[node]) for node in node_list if node not in S):
                        count += 1
                    return
                v = node_list[index]
                if not any(neighbor in S for neighbor in adj[v]):  # v not adjacent to any in S
                    # Can choose to add v or not
                    # Add v
                    S.add(v)
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
                    S.remove(v)
                    # Not add v
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
                else:
                    # Cannot add v, skip
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
            
            # Start backtracking with empty set
            backtrack(0, set())
            
            num_maximal_cocktails = count
            
            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,
                difficulty=message.difficulty,
                message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=num_maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
            )
        
        elif message.difficulty == 'normal':
            # List all maximal cocktails
            maximal_cocktails = []
            
            def backtrack(index, S):
                nonlocal maximal_cocktails
                if index == n:
                    # Check if S is maximal
                    if all(any(neighbor in S for neighbor in adj[node]) for node in node_list if node not in S):
                        # Add a sorted list of S
                        maximal_cocktails.append(sorted(list(S)))
                    return
                v = node_list[index]
                if not any(neighbor in S for neighbor in adj[v]):  # v not adjacent to any in S
                    # Can choose to add v or not
                    # Add v
                    S.add(v)
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
                    S.remove(v)
                    # Not add v
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
                else:
                    # Cannot add v, skip
                    backtrack(index + 1, S)
            
            # Start backtracking with empty set
            backtrack(0, set())
            
            return Info(
                sender=self.__class__.__name__,
                receiver=message.sender,
                difficulty=message.difficulty,
                message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=maximal_cocktails, type='custom')]
            )
